title: Adoption Sprint Playbook (30/60/90) - Draft
content:
Purpose: Rapidly align cross-functional teams around a repeatable 30/60/90 adoption sprint that drives usage, captures risk signals early, and produces QBR-ready artifacts for renewal conversations. This is a working draft — iterate after 2 live customer runs.

Context and audience:
- Primary audience: CS Managers + Solutions Engineers running post-sale onboarding for Redwood Hosted/Dedicated products.
- Secondary: Product Ops, Sales, SRE for escalations.

High-level objectives (customer-facing):
- 30d: Customer completes core integration, runs 3 representative workloads, and sees baseline latency/cost metrics.
- 60d: Customer adopts caching/batching recommendations, stabilizes infra, and hits defined SLA targets for p99 latency or throughput.
- 90d: Customer shows measurable feature usage (X daily active sessions or Y API calls/day), and a renewal risk score below threshold.

Success metrics (CS-owned):
- Integration completion: checklist 100% by day 30 (yes/no).
- Baseline throughput: tokens/sec or requests/min compared to target.
- Cost per 1k tokens delta after Optimize recommendations (target: >=10% improvement by day 60).
- NPS (mini-survey) at day 30 and day 90.

Risk signals (early flags) and scoring (quick heuristic):
- SIG1 (Critical): Cannot connect to model endpoints after 3 attempts, production blocking. +50 risk points.
- SIG2 (High): Customer hasn't executed any test calls by day 14. +30 risk points.
- SIG3 (Medium): Repeated quality regressions or hallucinations flagged in prompt evals. +15 risk points.
- SIG4 (Low): Feature requests backlog >3 items not acknowledged in 7d. +5 risk points.
- Thresholds: 0-19 green, 20-49 yellow (action required), 50+ red (escalate to SRE + AE).

Playbook: 0-30 days (Sprint 1) — Activate and baseline
- Goals: onboarding kickoff, credentials & VPC checks, basic integration, 3 smoke tests.
- Owner: CSM (execute), SE (technical), SRE on-call (as escalation).
- Key tasks:
  - Day 0: Kickoff meeting (30-45m) 
    - Agenda: success criteria, integration plan, sample workload, contacts, QBR cadence.
    - Deliverable: shared Confluence checklist link (linked_artifacts: CONFC-4829).
  - Day 3-7: Environment provisioning & auth validation.
  - Day 7-14: Baseline workload run (3 representative flows), capture latency and cost.
  - Day 14-21: First enablement session (function/tool-calling, streaming integration patterns).
  - Day 21-30: Run initial Optimize recommendations (simple batching + KV prefix cache). Record delta.
- Communication cadence: weekly 15m sync + async status in Slack.

Playbook: 31-60 days (Sprint 2) — Optimize and stabilize
- Goals: apply performance improvements, begin regular monitoring, plan for QBR content.
- Owner: SE + CSM.
- Key tasks:
  - Day 31-40: Apply batching/caching recommendations; perform quantization profile if requested.
  - Day 41-50: Load test representative peak; validate autoscaling behavior for Dedicated customers.
  - Day 51-60: Create first dashboard snapshots (token breakdown, p50/p95/p99, cost per route).
  - Align on QBR goals and success stories to capture.
- Communication cadence: biweekly progress updates, invite product for any feature gaps.

Playbook: 61-90 days (Sprint 3) — Adopt and prepare renewal narrative
- Goals: stabilize SLAs, demonstrate ROI gains, prepare QBR + renewal playbook.
- Owner: CSM (narrative), AE (commercial alignment), SE (technical validation).
- Key tasks:
  - Day 61-70: Run quality evals on prompt sets; compare to baseline.
  - Day 71-80: Draft QBR slide deck (see QBR template section). Include usage growth chart, cost savings from Optimize, latency improvements, outstanding risks.
  - Day 81-85: Internal pre-QBR with Sales + Product; align renewal ask.
  - Day 86-90: Present QBR to customer; propose renewal next steps if green.

QBR Template (one-page summary + 6 slides recommended):
- Slide 1: Executive summary: adoption status, headline metric (e.g., 18% cost reduction; 3x throughput).
- Slide 2: What we shipped: integration highlights and completed checklist items.
- Slide 3: Usage & performance: charts for tokens/day, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rate.
- Slide 4: Cost & unit economics: before/after optimize recommendations, projected monthly cost at steady state.
- Slide 5: Risks & mitigation plan: current risk score, actions taken, owners.
- Slide 6: Renewal proposal & recommended next steps (dedicated pool sizing, reserved capacity, roadmap asks).

Renewal trigger logic (CS-side quick rules):
- Auto-invite to renewal workflow if: 90-day NPS >= 7 OR usage growth >=25% quarter-over-quarter AND risk_score < 20.
- If risk_score 20-49: require remediation plan + AE involvement; pause auto-renewal.
- If risk_score >=50: immediate escalation to VP CS and Sales for churn prevention.

Renewal tracker (sample table - paste into sheet):
- Columns (customer, renewal-date, renewal-owner, current-mrr, usage-trend, risk-score, next-action)
- Example row: "Acme AI", "2026-07-15", "Marisa Chen", "$24,000", "+32%", "14", "QBR scheduled 2026-03-20"

Templates: short kickoff email (to send Day 0)
- Subject: "Redwood kickoff: [Customer] onboarding plan + quick sync"
- Body (short): "Thanks again for choosing Redwood. Quick 30m to align success criteria and contacts. Agenda includes integration plan, sample workload, and QBR cadence. Proposed time: [slot]."

Enablement checklist (CS internal shorthand):
- API keys validated, VPC peering (if required), sample app calls succeed, prompt eval harness configured, cost dashboard created, alerting configured on p99 and error rate.

Escalation paths (names are examples):
- 0-24h: CSM + SE on Slack for triage.
- 24-72h: SRE on-call engaged (pager).
- >72h or critical outage: Escalate to Infrastructure Lead (Owen Li) and VP CS.

Notes & open questions (working):
- Need a compact ‘integrations health’ badge for dashboards — ask product if we can add 1-line status API for each customer. (ACTION: Priya to open feature request CONFC-5122)
- Ticketing: prefer JIRA epic per customer for technical tasks; add CS checklist as sub-tasks.

Recommended next steps before this doc goes final:
- Run this playbook on 3 customers (mix hosted and dedicated) and capture deviations.
- Capture templates into Google Slides / Confluence for reuse.

Quick references (internal links and IDs):
- Confluence adoption checklist: CONFC-4829
- Current onboarding backlog epic: JIRA-CS-1734
- Slack channel: #cs-onboarding

Last thoughts (notes-to-self style):
- Keep the 30d enablement very hands-on; automation helps later but early wins are people-driven.
- Avoid over-indexing on raw API calls — focus on customer-defined success events.
- Keep QBR deck crisp; execs want a 1-minute headline and clear dollar impact.

---
Change log (draft history):
- 2025-11-21: initial outline (Marisa Chen)
- 2026-01-14: added risk scoring heuristic + renewal triggers (Diego Ramirez)
- 2026-03-01: tuned checklist and QBR slide list; minor wording edits (Priya Nair)

End of draft.
